slides.title: New Onboarding: Value Before Profile
slides.subtitle: A proposal to let users experience value first
body: Framing the onboarding problem for team and leads
slides.notes: This proposal opens with a clear problem: new users struggle to find the core feature. We will frame why onboarding order matters, then present a direction, illustrative comparison, plan, and the decision we are asking for.

slides.title: Users Struggle to Find the Core Feature
slides.subtitle: The core user problem
body: New users struggle to locate the core feature
This friction undermines early engagement
We must reduce time-to-value in onboarding
slides.notes: The background is straightforward: new users struggle to find the core feature. This friction slows early engagement and risks drop-off before users ever see what the product can do for them.

slides.title: Show Product Value Before Profile Setup
slides.subtitle: Proposed direction
body: Let users experience product value first
Defer profile information until after value is clear
Reduce setup friction at the start of onboarding
Align onboarding flow with the core feature
slides.notes: The goal is to let users experience product value before completing profile information. By deferring profile setup, we reduce initial friction and guide users toward the core feature sooner.

slides.title: Illustrative Completion Rates: 42% vs 68%
slides.subtitle: Demo figures only, not actual business statistics
body: Legacy flow completion: 42%
Pilot flow completion: 68%
Illustrative dataset for direction comparison
Not a substitute for real business metrics
slides.notes: These figures come from an illustrative dataset only. The legacy flow shows a 42% completion rate, while the pilot flow shows 68%. They are demo figures, not actual business statistics, and should be treated as directional evidence for the proposal rather than a performance claim. The gap suggests the proposed direction is worth piloting and measuring with real data.

slides.title: Four-Week Plan: Research to Evaluation
slides.subtitle: A tight four-week cycle from insight to decision
body: Week 1｜Research: map user friction and core-feature discovery
Week 2｜Prototype: build value-first onboarding flow
Week 3｜Pilot: run with a limited user cohort
Week 4｜Evaluation: review results and recommend next step
slides.notes: The plan runs over four weeks. Week one focuses on research to understand where users struggle. Week two builds a prototype of the value-first flow. Week three runs a limited pilot, and week four evaluates results to inform the go-forward decision. This keeps the proposal scoped, fast, and measurable.

slides.title: Decision: Approve Direction and Pilot Scope
slides.subtitle: What we need from leadership today
body: Approve the value-before-profile direction
Confirm pilot scope and target cohort
Align on four-week timeline and checkpoints
Agree success criteria before kickoff
slides.notes: We are asking for two decisions today: approval of the value-before-profile direction, and confirmation of the pilot scope. Once approved, we will align on the four-week timeline and agree on success criteria before kickoff. This keeps the team focused and gives leadership a clear checkpoint at the end of the pilot.
